paragraphs: Mentioned in Sukkah 26b: Rabbi Eliezer spent the Sabbath in the Upper Galilee in Yochanan ben Ilai's sukkah, in Kisri; some say Kisrin.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Kisri and Kisrin preserve the two supplied place-name forms; neither is silently replaced by a modern location.

The consulted event appears in Sukkah 27b: Rabbi Eliezer stays in the sukkah of Yochanan beRabbi Ilai, at Kisri or Kisrayon. Hyman’s 26b locator and Kisrin variant remain unchanged. The passage titles the father Ilai, not Yochanan; the display title therefore follows the supplied Yochanan ben Ilai heading without adding Rabbi.
